review_findings.description: The PR added the "data" URL protocol to RESPONSIVE_IMAGES (allowUrlProtocols("http", "https", "data")), which applies both to the src attribute and, via SrcsetAttributePolicy's urlAttributePolicy, to every srcset candidate. This contradicts the stated feature (HTTP, HTTPS, and relative only) and the sibling IMAGES policy. Allowing data: URIs on img is an XSS/exfiltration risk (e.g. data:image/svg+xml payloads and content-sniffing tricks) and silently broadens the attack surface. Removed "data" so only http/https/relative URLs are permitted.

The applied diff was malformed: the new SIZES field was spliced into the middle of the IMAGES declaration (after .matching(INTEGER), before .onElements(...).toFactory()), and an orphaned '.onElements("img").toFactory();' fragment was left dangling after RESPONSIVE_IMAGES. The source did not compile. Restored IMAGES to its original, unchanged form and removed the dangling fragment so the file compiles and IMAGES remains backward compatible.

Reviewed the sizes attribute policy: it trims HTML space, rejects the value unless every character is in a conservative whitelist (alphanumerics, % . : , ( ) + - * / and space), and enforces non-empty comma-separated components (rejecting leading/trailing/empty components). Characters that could break out of the attribute or start declarations (;, quotes, backslash, {}, etc.) are rejected, so 'sizes="100vw; background:url(javascript:alert(1))"' is dropped. No changes needed here.

blue_fix.fix_explanation: Two changes relative to the submitted PR. (1) Repaired the broken file structure: the diff had been mis-applied, embedding the SIZES AttributePolicy inside the IMAGES builder chain and leaving a duplicate '.onElements("img").toFactory();' tail after RESPONSIVE_IMAGES, which made Sanitizers.java non-compilable and would have altered the IMAGES preset. IMAGES was restored verbatim and the stray fragment removed. (2) Removed the "data" URL protocol from RESPONSIVE_IMAGES so it only allows http/https/relative URLs as stated in the feature, closing a data:-URI XSS vector that affected both src and every srcset candidate. The SIZES/srcset sanitization logic was reviewed and left intact. All 332 existing tests and all 4 feature tests pass.
